Business goal: Create a new proposed durable design-system page through governed topology instead of ad hoc repo edits.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can add a new design-system page in the page tree and prepare it for preview/apply materialization.
Notes / constraints: This capability is create-only for v1 and must not invent page-local CSS or arbitrary feature behavior. Folder creation is allowed later during apply, but folder movement is not part of this create flow. The approved v1 template key is `static-html-page`.
Tenant context rule: root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may create proposed design-system pages.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may show create actions. Hidden or disabled UI does not replace backend enforcement.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before proposed create. The feature must validate parent placement displayLabel routeSegment and required template key `static-html-page`, reject system-managed fields, and create only proposed topology truth.
Frontend states: create draft, validation error, proposed success, denied state
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may hide or disable create when permission is missing but must not replace backend enforcement.
Request contract: Body supplies allowed topology inputs only: parent placement displayLabel routeSegment and required template key `static-html-page`.
Response contract: Returns proposed page identity placement summary and current proposal status without writing repo files yet.
Error contract: 400 invalid input unsupported template key or duplicate sibling segment; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 parent not found; 409 invalid placement or duplicate conflict.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes discovery-owned family knowledge from `webAppSurfaceDiscovery` only through public reads when needed for family validation.
Persistence impact: Adds proposed-topology state for a design-system page. No repo materialization yet.
Indexes / uniqueness: Normalized sibling route-segment uniqueness within the approved parent scope. Stable proposed/applied identity keys are required if the same row later becomes applied truth.
Search / filter model: Exact and scoped reads only in v1. No broad fuzzy search required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Create is additive in v1. No route retirement redirect or folder-move behavior should be implied by this capability.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local create validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing same-origin admin/operator surface. Later browser flow should stay inside approved CSP rules.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through existing shared authz audit visibility. Success-side audit is recommended if topology mutation is treated as a privileged operator action.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal topology metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are high because this creates durable proposed topology truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when an operator can create a proposed design-system page through governed inputs only, without repo mutation or invented behavior.

Business goal: Create a new proposed child page beneath an existing design-system page through governed topology.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can add a subpage under an approved parent and see it reflected in proposed topology.
Notes / constraints: This is the child-page variant of proposed page create. It must preserve explicit parent-child placement and reject unsupported parent kinds or invalid placement. The approved v1 template key is `static-html-page`.
Tenant context rule: root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may create proposed design-system subpages.
Authz scope type: root-scoped proposed topology create under an exact parent
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may show subpage-create actions. Hidden UI is not sufficient enforcement.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before proposed subpage create. The feature must validate the exact parent, child placement, normalized segment uniqueness, and required template key `static-html-page`.
Frontend states: create child draft, validation error, proposed success, denied state
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side UI may disable create-child affordances but backend remains authoritative.
Request contract: Body supplies exact parentPageId displayLabel routeSegment and required template key `static-html-page` only.
Response contract: Returns proposed child identity plus explicit parent-child placement summary.
Error contract: 400 invalid input unsupported template key or duplicate child segment; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 parent not found; 409 unsupported placement.
Cross-feature seams: May consume discovery-owned family structure for validation only through public seams.
Persistence impact: Adds proposed-topology state for a design-system child page. No repo materialization yet.
Indexes / uniqueness: Normalized child-segment uniqueness under the same parent. Stable proposed/applied identity rules should remain consistent with page create.
Search / filter model: Exact and scoped reads only in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Subpage create is additive in v1 and must not trigger folder moves or route retirement semantics.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local create validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing approved operator surface.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through existing shared authz audit visibility. Success-side audit is recommended if topology mutation is treated as privileged.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal topology metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance remain high.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when an operator can create a proposed child page under an approved parent through governed inputs only and the parent-child topology remains explicit.

Business goal: Show what repo changes would occur for a proposed design-system topology change before any apply happens.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can inspect whether a change is additive compatibility-sensitive blocked or invalid and see the deterministic planned repo outputs before apply.
Notes / constraints: Preview must be no-mutation. It must not write repo files, must classify blocked folder moves honestly, and must treat route-segment rename as compatibility-sensitive.
Tenant context rule: root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may preview design-system materialization.
Authz scope type: root-scoped preview over proposed topology changes
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose preview/apply affordances.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before preview. The feature must compare proposed and applied truth and return deterministic planned materialization outputs and classification without mutating persistence or repo files.
Frontend states: preview pending, preview summary, compatibility-sensitive warning, blocked state, invalid state
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side preview UI is advisory only; backend owns final classification.
Request contract: Body identifies exact proposed change scope or selected proposal ids plus approved preview flags. Clients cannot submit raw file-write plans.
Response contract: Returns preview summary with classification additive compatibility-sensitive blocked or invalid plus planned repo outputs such as folder create index.html create no behavior module stub for `static-html-page` and lightweight governance stub create at `docs/workspace/design-system/generated-pages/<page-slug>.md`.
Error contract: 400 invalid scope preview flags or unsupported template key; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 proposal or parent not found; 409 blocked materialization or stale preview state.
Cross-feature seams: May read current discovery-owned design-system truth through `webAppSurfaceDiscovery` when needed to keep family posture honest.
Persistence impact: Read-only compare across proposed truth applied truth and current family posture. No repo or applied mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on proposal ids parent ids proposal status and route-segment uniqueness support deterministic preview lookup.
Search / filter model: Preview by explicit proposal scope only. No broad fuzzy preview surface in the first slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Route-segment rename is compatibility-sensitive. Folder movement and delete/retire remain blocked in v1. No redirects or aliases are invented implicitly.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local preview validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the approved operator surface.
Audit requirement: Audit denied preview attempts through existing shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is recommended if preview is treated as privileged review activity.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; exposes internal topology and planned repo-change metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift importance are high because preview is the safety boundary before repo mutation.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when an operator can inspect a deterministic no-mutation preview that clearly shows what repo files would be created and whether the change is additive or blocked.

Business goal: Apply an approved design-system topology change so curated applied truth and repo scaffolding are created intentionally.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can confirm a previewed change and have the page tree and repo scaffold update through one governed flow.
Notes / constraints: Apply must be deterministic. It may create a folder index.html no behavior module stub by default for `static-html-page` and a lightweight governance stub at `docs/workspace/design-system/generated-pages/<page-slug>.md`. It must not create page-local CSS by default and must not silently move folders.
Tenant context rule: root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may apply design-system topology materialization.
Authz scope type: root-scoped apply over an approved preview scope
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose the final confirmation action.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before apply. The feature must validate preview freshness validate the requested apply scope write applied topology truth execute materialization and return the refreshed applied tree or explicit failure without hidden partial success.
Frontend states: apply confirm, apply success, apply failure, post-apply refreshed tree
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side confirmation is not sufficient; backend must reject stale or blocked apply attempts.
Request contract: Body identifies an approved preview or selected proposal ids plus allowed apply posture flags. Clients cannot submit raw file-write instructions.
Response contract: Returns apply summary with created repo outputs updated applied topology ids lightweight governance stub path `docs/workspace/design-system/generated-pages/<page-slug>.md` and the refreshed page tree or tree reference.
Error contract: 400 invalid apply scope or flags; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 proposal/preview not found; 409 stale preview blocked folder move blocked delete unsupported template key or incompatible materialization state.
Cross-feature seams: May read discovery-owned family truth through public seams to keep applied posture honest; must not import frontend implementation internals directly into backend domain logic.
Persistence impact: Writes applied topology truth and materialization metadata and creates repo scaffold outputs for the approved design-system page or subpage.
Indexes / uniqueness: Stable proposal-to-applied linkage and route-segment uniqueness remain required. Additional indexes may be needed on apply status or last-applied metadata if persisted.
Search / filter model: Apply by exact approved preview or selected proposal ids only. No broad fuzzy mutation surface in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Apply is compatibility-sensitive when route-segment rename is involved. Folder moves and delete/retire remain blocked in v1. No implicit redirect or alias generation.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local apply validation and conflict detection.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the approved operator surface. Materialized pages should rely on existing shared system CSS posture by default.
Audit requirement: Audit denied apply attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is recommended because this is a privileged topology and repo-mutation action.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; persists internal topology/materialization metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization migration safety and anti-drift importance are all high because this capability changes durable applied truth and writes repo scaffolding.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when an operator can intentionally materialize a previewed design-system page or subpage through one governed flow and the tree refreshes from applied truth immediately afterward.

Business goal: Read the current applied design-system topology so the page tree reflects what has actually been accepted and materialized.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can see the applied page tree immediately after create/preview/apply workflows without relying on client-side guesses.
Notes / constraints: This read should use a workflow-specific route rather than silently changing the broader tree contract. It should reflect applied truth, not merely proposed drafts, and should support immediate refresh after successful apply.
Tenant context rule: root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may read the applied design-system topology tree through the protected workflow.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose the materialization workflow tree when it is protected.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before reads. The feature must return applied tree truth deterministically after successful apply and must not confuse proposed-only pages with applied pages unless the contract explicitly includes proposal posture.
Frontend states: loading, applied tree loaded, empty, error, denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may hide the tree when permission is missing but backend remains authoritative.
Request contract: No broad fuzzy search in v1. Query should stay explicit and workflow-specific for applied-tree reads.
Response contract: Returns deterministic applied tree truth with enough node metadata to refresh the operator page tree after apply without changing the broader `GET /v1/web-app-hierarchy/tree` contract.
Cross-feature seams: May later compare against discovery-owned truth through separate preview flows but the read itself remains hierarchy-owned.
Persistence impact: Read-only access to current applied topology truth. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Existing tree indexes and ordering rules remain important. Additional applied-tree filters may require additive indexes if introduced.
Search / filter model: Explicit list/read filters only. Avoid broad fuzzy search in the first slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: This read is the immediate post-apply truth source. It should not silently change route semantics or infer folder movement.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local read validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the approved operator surface.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads through shared authz visibility if the workflow remains privileged.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; exposes internal topology metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift importance are high because this read is the operator-visible confirmation of applied truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when the operator tree refreshes from applied truth immediately after a successful materialization flow and does not depend on hidden background reconciliation.
